why: In each row, figure 1 minus figure 2 gives figure 3. Row 1: (right, left, right) minus (left) leaves two right arrows. Row 3 removes the fork-line and the dot-line. Row 2 needs: figure 1 minus two left arrows = two right arrows, so figure 1 has 2 right arrows outside and 2 left arrows inside, like row 1. Option 3 matches; option 1 has the arrows in a different order.
trick: Try "first minus second = third" when the last figure is simpler than the first.
note: Option 1 also has 2 right and 2 left arrows; option 3 is chosen because it keeps the right arrows on the outside like row 1, which matches the book key.
